blindSummary: No criminalisation of trans presence. This state/province's legislature created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure by a civil-code amendment in 2021; after the country's highest court ruled in June 2023 that excluding children and adolescents was unconstitutional, a 2024 reform expanded the right. The unit also recognises the transfemicide offence. No region-specific incident or enforcement pattern was found, so visitor-facing risk is inherited from the country's documented position.
blindSourceSummaries: A major human-rights organisation's state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition (March 2025), covering which of the country's 32 states/provinces have legislated an administrative procedure and the highest court rulings that drove expansion. For this unit: a 2021 civil-code amendment created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure; a 2024 reform expanded it to children and adolescents after the June 2023 court ruling.

A major human-rights organisation's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring state/province: the absence of a legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional maltreatment - the August 2023 killing of a trans activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that state/province's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. A baseline for how a non-reforming state/province behaves.

A major newspaper report (24 July 2024) on the national capital district making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (approved 18 July 2024), in one of the deadliest settings for trans people in the region; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2021/2024 legal gender recognition reforms and recognition of the transfemicide offence are resident-facing civil-registry and criminal-law machinery.
